exposure: pregnancy status (before, after, or coinciding with disease onset)
disease type (ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease)
cohort: 406 women with ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease aged 18-45 years
finding: While pregnant women with UC had better long-term disease courses compared to non-pregnant women, those whose pregnancy coincided with disease onset experienced worse disease courses, and pregnancies after disease onset were associated with more cesarean sections and adverse fetal outcomes in both UC and CD patients.
mod_finding: Pregnancies after disease onset (UC or CD) were associated with more cesarean sections compared to pregnancies before disease onset.
